status: Confirmed AI provenance and deployed use; NMC jurisdiction conditional
title: Synthetic doctor and consultation photographs are presented as real practice scenes
location: design/handoff/IMAGE-MAP.md:9-18; app/about-dr-james/page.tsx:74-80; components/home/HowHeWorks.tsx:99-111; app/contact/page.tsx:49-56; lib/conditions.ts:227-259; app/conditions/[slug]/page.tsx:89-96; app/your-visit/page.tsx:130-131; app/conditions/page.tsx:65-66; app/health-library/page.tsx:95-96
quoted_text: Image map: 'd03-consultation.jpg ... AI ... Dr. James explaining a care plan to a patient during a consultation'; 'd01-hero.jpg ... AI'; deployed alt text: 'Dr. James showing a patient a blood glucose reading'; home caption: 'In clinic ... Badr Al Samaa Royal Hospital'.
why: Documented synthetic depictions of the actual RMP and patient interactions, described as real clinical scenes, risk the misleading representation prohibited by 7.2; merely adding an AI label does not cure a prohibited representation.
alternative: Remove the rendered d01-hero, d03-consultation, d05-results, d06-corridor, d07-welcome, d08-blood-sugar, d09-blood-pressure and d10-lungs image families from their existing page slots, including the Your Visit stepper and condition-group panels; remove associated clinical-scene captions and alt text. Leave the existing factual text and navigation. Do not replace them with generated people. Do not classify the currently imported d02-hero-cutout as AI solely from the older image map's d01-cutout entry: the current hero uses a different asset. For any independently confirmed AI-generated non-person educational illustrations that are retained, show 'AI-generated illustration; not a patient image.' This last instruction is conditional, not a finding that every library cover is AI.
seo_aeo: Preserve the condition text, headings, internal links and genuine reviewer credentials; removing synthetic clinical scenes need not remove the page or its search intent. Update image metadata rather than leaving false clinical alt text.
client_input: Confirm asset provenance and approve removal of the documented synthetic scenes. Approval of an image by the doctor is not an exception to the prohibition.

status: JUDGEMENT on promotional context; not a blanket ban on identification photos
title: Doctor imagery is used in promotional hero, biography and share-card placements
quoted_text: Hero: 'A physician who sees the whole picture.'; 'Book a consultation'; portrait alt: 'Dr. James Kumar Pallivathukkal, Specialist Internist, in a white coat with arms crossed'. OG source: 'd04-headshot-800sq.jpg', followed by the doctor's name and role.
why: The combination of dominant portraits, personal positioning, credential/stat panels and booking prompts is materially different from a plain identification photograph and raises self-publicity risk under 9.2.
alternative: Low-risk option: remove doctor photographs from home hero, promotional home biography panel, inner-page banners and default OG/Twitter share card; keep one genuine plain identification photograph on About beside verified credentials and registration. Replace the hero slogan with 'Internal Medicine and Diabetes consultations in Muscat.' Follow with 'Badr Al Samaa Royal Hospital, Al Ghubrah Street. Saturday to Thursday, 9 am to 1 pm and 5 pm to 9 pm. Appointments: +968 9751 0975.' Keep the share card text-only, with the page title, doctor name and location. Small reviewer-identification headshots are lower-risk JUDGEMENT, not separately counted prohibited photographs. NMC-001 separately addresses synthetic imagery; do not duplicate removal work.
seo_aeo: Keep textual identity, qualifications, location and Physician schema. A genuine profile identification image can retain entity association without promotional portrait banners.
client_input: Approval of the conservative photo-placement policy; qualified local advice if the practice wants to retain borderline placements.

status: Confirmed public marketing credit; payment model not established
title: Three public surfaces explicitly describe third-party medical marketing
quoted_text: 'Built & Marketed by Automize Media Labs'; 'Website built and marketed by Automize Media Labs'; 'Built & marketed by: Automize Media Labs'.
why: These credits expressly describe the third-party marketing engagement barred by 8.1(ii), rather than merely identifying a website developer.
alternative: Remove the marketing credits from all three surfaces. A neutral 'Website: Automize Media Labs' credit is appropriate only if it truthfully describes lawful technical website work. Review and stop any prohibited medical-service promotion or patient-procurement arrangement itself; changing or concealing the credit while continuing prohibited marketing is not a compliant fix. Do not infer a referral-fee arrangement from generic analytics event names alone.
seo_aeo: The practice's medical entity, citations and clinical content do not depend on the agency credit. Remove the marketing statement from the machine-readable text as well as the visible footer.
client_input: Agency statement of work, confirmation of whether services are limited to technical/informational work, and whether any payment depends on leads or patients.

status: MISSING against requested benchmark; Indian RMP applicability must be confirmed
title: The named physician has no published registration number, council or registration status
quoted_text: Site name: 'Dr. James Kumar Pallivathukkal'; qualifications include 'MBBS', 'MD', 'PG Dip'; source value: mohLicence: '[CONFIRM: number]'. The rendered profile, footer and Physician graph disclose no council/registration number or status.
why: For an RMP subject to the NMC framework, identity and qualifications without registration status and SMR/NMR number do not meet Explanation III; the practice's Indian registration and jurisdiction are not established by this site.
alternative: Obtain verified registration evidence first. If Indian registration applies, use: 'Dr. James Kumar Pallivathukkal, MBBS, MD (Internal Medicine), PG Diploma in Diabetes. Registered with [verified council name]; SMR/NMR Registration No. [verified number]; status: [verified current status].' Also show the verified Oman Ministry of Health professional licence where applicable, clearly distinguished from Indian registration. Use the verified disclosure in the profile, footer and medical bylines; mirror it as an appropriate identifier/credential in schema. The bracketed fields are a controlled client-input template, not publishable copy; never invent values or infer the council from where he studied. If he has no applicable Indian registration, do not invent one or label him an Indian RMP; obtain a documented jurisdiction decision and publish the applicable verified Oman licensing information.
seo_aeo: Verified identifiers strengthen entity disambiguation and credential trust. Do not fabricate structured-data identifiers or imply that an Oman licence is an SMR/NMR number.
client_input: Oman licence and current status; whether he retains Indian registration; exact council, SMR/NMR number and status if applicable; confirmation of the applicable professional regulator.

status: Confirmed absolute diagnostic/service claims; not a finding of a guaranteed cure
title: Absolute wording promises diagnostic completeness and error-free testing
quoted_text: 'Dr. James always finds the cause before treating'; 'hidden blood loss is ruled out'; 'A simple blood test gives the answer'; 'no wasted tests'; 'nothing doubled up and nothing missed'; 'so nothing is added that clashes with something else'.
why: These unqualified assurances of diagnostic certainty and omission-free care create expectations that cannot be guaranteed for an individual consultation.
alternative: Anaemia intro: 'Anaemia means the blood carries less oxygen than usual. Assessment looks for possible causes and guides treatment; further investigation or referral may be needed.' Anaemia assessment: replace 'hidden blood loss is ruled out when the pattern demands it' with 'possible hidden blood loss is investigated when indicated'; after-visit paragraph: 'The findings, likely causes, treatment options and follow-up plan are discussed. Further tests or referral may be needed if the cause remains uncertain.' Thyroid intro: replace the final sentence with 'Blood tests help assess thyroid function; interpretation depends on symptoms, medicines and other findings.' Home testing principle: 'Tests are selected according to the clinical assessment.' Home medicines line: 'A medicines review checks for duplication, interactions and suitability.' Home check-up line: 'Tests are selected after a consultation, based on your history.' Older-adult FAQ: replace the final sentence with 'A medicines review helps assess possible interactions and duplication across the treatment plan.' Diabetes follow-up: replace the final sentence with 'Kidney, eye and cholesterol checks are arranged according to your clinical needs.' Preventive-check-up intro: 'A check-up starts with a consultation. Tests are selected according to your age, family history, symptoms and other risk factors.' Apply the revised strings to their FAQ schema/metadata derivatives rather than leaving older promises there.
seo_aeo: Keep condition names and answer-first explanations. Qualified factual language remains useful for snippets and avoids promising a guaranteed clinical outcome.
client_input: Doctor approval of the replacement clinical wording.

status: MISSING balanced risk/limitations information in the listed existing treatment descriptions
title: Several short treatment descriptions give benefits or reassurance without balanced treatment risks
quoted_text: Thyroid: 'a daily hormone tablet long-term, which is safe and works well'; asthma: 'untreated asthma is far riskier than the medicine'; sleep apnea: 'usually needs a CPAP machine, which keeps the airway open'; weight: 'whether a medicine suits your situation'; diabetes: 'Insulin is added only when the body needs it'; anaemia: 'tablets help'.
why: These existing treatment explanations are insufficiently balanced under the brief's M3 standard; a footer disclaimer does not explain treatment-specific adverse effects or variable response.
alternative: Doctor-review-ready text for the existing sections: Thyroid: 'Underactive thyroid is often treated with thyroid hormone replacement. The dose needs monitoring: too much can cause palpitations and other problems, while too little may leave symptoms unresolved. The need for treatment and response vary. Overactive thyroid has different treatment options and risks, which should be discussed individually.' Asthma: 'Preventer inhalers help many people control asthma when used as prescribed. Depending on the inhaler, side effects can include a sore mouth, hoarseness or tremor. Technique, dose and monitoring matter, and control varies. Do not change treatment without medical advice.' CPAP: 'CPAP helps keep the airway open during sleep. Mask discomfort, nasal dryness, skin irritation or air leakage can occur. Suitability, comfort and response vary, and follow-up may be needed.' Weight management: 'Weight-loss medicines are suitable for some people, not everyone. Benefits, contraindications and side effects depend on the medicine; gastrointestinal symptoms and other adverse effects can occur. Results vary and monitoring is needed.' Diabetes: 'Treatment may include lifestyle measures, tablets or insulin, depending on assessment. Some diabetes medicines, including insulin, can cause low blood sugar; other risks depend on the medicine. Targets and response vary, and doses need monitoring.' Iron treatment: 'Iron tablets may help when iron deficiency is confirmed. They can cause nausea, abdominal discomfort, constipation or dark stools, and can interact with other medicines. Response varies; follow-up blood tests check progress and investigation of the cause may still be needed.' Place the relevant text next to the treatment discussion and update corresponding FAQ answers. These are edits to existing treatments, not recommendations to add services. The longer weight-loss-injection guide already discusses risks and varying outcomes and is not reported as missing them.
seo_aeo: Retain the treatment questions and improve balanced answers. Do not blanket-delete educational treatment content or duplicate a generic risk paragraph across unrelated pages.
client_input: Doctor review of each risk statement and confirmation that it matches the treatment actually discussed.

clause: 7.6 to the extent applicable/in force; audit brief M2
status: Confirmed incomplete privacy-notice identity; consent checkbox and policy link already exist
title: The privacy notice hides an unresolved operator identity
quoted_text: Rendered policy: 'This website is operated by ("we", "us").' Source: 'This website is operated by [CONFIRM: Dr James personally or a company]'; retention: 'kept for 12 months by default ... [CONFIRM: retention agreed with client]'.
why: The existing notice names no operator after its placeholder is stripped, so a visitor cannot clearly identify who is responsible for the appointment data despite the other notice and consent controls being present.
alternative: After verifying the actual operator, replace the first sentence with 'This website is operated by [verified legal operator name], responsible for the personal information collected through this website. Privacy enquiries and complaints: omanjamesp@gmail.com, +968 9751 0975.' If Dr. James personally is confirmed as the operator, the complete name is 'Dr. James Kumar Pallivathukkal'; otherwise use the actual legal entity, not an assumed name. Keep the existing unticked consent checkbox and privacy-policy link. Retain the 12-month retention statement only after the client confirms the actual deletion process, including inbox/provider copies; if it is not true, replace it with the verified retention period and exceptions. Do not publish bracketed fields. Do not remove or change data-processing safeguards silently as a copy fix.
seo_aeo: Completing the existing policy preserves its URL and trust function; no new marketing feature or structured-data expansion is needed.
client_input: Legal operator, actual retention/deletion practice, privacy grievance owner, email/hosting processor arrangements and cross-border safeguards. This is not a finding that retention or a contact address is absent.

status: Confirmed publication/review-claim mismatch; actual off-repository sign-off unknown
title: Condition pages publish without recorded sign-off but still emit reviewedBy schema
quoted_text: Policy: 'AI-assisted drafting is never published without human medical review'; condition route comment: 'the page still ships either way'; schema helper: reviewedBy: { '@id': ... '#dr-james' }. All 18 condition files lack recorded status/reviewedBy/reviewedOn values; sampled deployed condition graphs still assert reviewedBy.
why: The declared AI/editorial safeguard is not enforced for condition publication, while machine-readable review attribution is emitted independently of the recorded approval state.
alternative: Obtain and record genuine doctor sign-off for each existing condition page before public release. Until then, keep the affected pages restricted as drafts rather than merely hiding their review warning in a production-mode preview. Gate condition publication and reviewedBy/lastReviewed output on the same verified approval state used for guides; never set status or dates merely to pass a check. Keep the factual AI-assisted drafting disclosure. Change the llms.txt guide description from 'plain-language guides written and reviewed by Dr. James' to 'plain-language health guides medically reviewed by Dr. James', but only for guides with verified approval. The source for that phrase is app/llms.txt/route.ts:32. Existing frontmatter claims on the 62 guides still require genuine sign-off records; this audit does not prove those claims false.

client_input: Doctor approval records/dates for the 18 condition pages and confirmation of the guide-review records; confirmation of actual AI assistance.

status: JUDGEMENT: record association and certificate caption need substantiation
title: A personal record/achievement presentation is not independently substantiated by the displayed certificate
quoted_text: 'Associated with a Guinness World Records achievement for maximum diabetes patient screening at Badr Al Samaa Royal Hospital, 2025'; image alt: 'Dr. James holding his Guinness World Records certificate'.
why: The record association is used as personal promotional proof, but the displayed certificate photograph does not establish the claimed Guinness record, holder, event date or the doctor's precise role.
alternative: Low-risk exact change: remove the 'Diabetes screening record' milestone on Home and About and the certificate photograph/caption used to substantiate it; retain the existing factual employment and training chronology. Do not relabel another certificate as Guinness evidence. If the client later supplies an independently verifiable record and exact role, have the proposed factual attribution reviewed under 8.1(iii)/(ix) before retaining anything; do not convert an institutional record into an individual clinical-success claim. No recommendation to add an awards section.
seo_aeo: Existing verified qualifications and employment retain the expertise signal. Avoid search/AI amplification of an ambiguous award-holder association.
client_input: Official record/event reference, record holder, date and doctor's documented role if the claim is to be retained; identity of the certificate actually photographed.

status: JUDGEMENT on cumulative promotional framing, not a ban on factual appointments or emergency advice
title: Educational articles repeatedly shift into named-doctor promotion and booking
quoted_text: 'Book an appointment ... Book one ... Book one'; 'If you live in Muscat and your readings have been worrying you, Dr. James Pallivathukkal can review them with you'; template: 'Book a consultation'; closer: 'Talk to Dr. James about ...'.
why: Repeated named-doctor pitches and booking inserts within and after educational advice can turn an otherwise informational article into personal solicitation; contextual assessment is required.
alternative: Replace the blood-pressure appointment paragraph with 'If you have not had a recent blood pressure measurement, ask a healthcare professional when to check it. Repeated elevated readings should be assessed. Very high readings or symptoms such as chest pain, severe breathlessness or new neurological symptoms need urgent medical assessment rather than a routine booking.' Replace its promotional final sentence with 'Keep a record of readings and discuss the pattern with a qualified healthcare professional.' Replace the GLP-1 guide's named-doctor final paragraph with 'Response to GLP-1 treatment varies. Discuss expected benefits, risks, monitoring and what happens if treatment stops with a qualified healthcare professional.' Remove repeated personal promotional sign-offs and in-body booking sentences from existing guides while retaining their medical disclaimers. In the guide template, retain factual related-condition/visit links but remove the embedded booking row and the repeated doctor-promotion closing band. Keep one ordinary site navigation/contact route and the genuine reviewer attribution. Do not weaken appropriate emergency warnings.
seo_aeo: Retain clinical headings, answers, sources, internal educational links and genuine bylines. Removing repeated sales inserts does not require removing local practice information from the contact/profile pages.
client_input: Approval of the conservative educational/contact separation and doctor review of emergency advice.

clause: 7.6 to the extent applicable/in force; existing privacy-policy consent promise
status: Confirmed source defect and isolated test; dormant unless GA is configured and previously accepted
title: Withdrawing analytics consent does not stop an already-loaded GA instance
quoted_text: track(): 'if (!loaded && !loadGa()) return'; pageView(): 'if (!loaded || !window.gtag || !GA_ID) return'; consent handler only calls loadGa() when analytics is true. Policy: 'Withdraw consent for analytics at any time'.
why: Consent is checked at initial loading but not at later event dispatch, so previously enabled analytics continues after the stored preference changes to declined.
alternative: Recheck analyticsAllowed() before every track() and pageView() dispatch. On withdrawal, stop further measurement, update the vendor consent state/disable analytics and clear applicable analytics cookies; on re-acceptance, restore measurement only after a fresh permission check. Do not rely only on removing a script element. Preserve default refusal and the existing settings link. Acceptance check: accept, withdraw, navigate and click ordinary contact links in a synthetic test; no further measurement requests should occur until re-acceptance.
seo_aeo: No search-content loss; analytics totals may decrease to reflect actual permission. Consent enforcement is not an SEO ranking workaround.
client_input: Whether GA will be enabled at launch, measurement/property configuration and cookie inventory. No GA requests were observed before consent on the inspected preview; this is not a claim of an actual user-data breach.

status: Confirmed payload design and inaccurate assurance; no actual personal-data transmission established
title: Analytics retains arbitrary UTM values and health-topic paths despite categorical anonymous/no-health-data copy
quoted_text: URL cleaning: 'if (k.startsWith("utm_")) keep.set(k, v)'; payload: page_path: window.location.pathname; notice: 'No ads, no health data'; policy: 'This is anonymous and never includes health information'.
why: Unrestricted campaign values can contain identifiers and condition-page paths reveal health-related browsing interests, so the implementation does not support an absolute promise of anonymous, health-information-free measurement.
alternative: Before enabling GA, remove arbitrary query values from measurement and use only a controlled set of non-personal campaign codes if needed; do not collect condition-specific paths/titles, full referrers, outbound WhatsApp messages or booking fields. Audit vendor automatic/enhanced measurement as well as custom events. Low-risk option: keep optional GA disabled until that configuration is verified. Replace cookie copy with 'We use essential storage to run the site. If you choose optional analytics, it helps us understand website use. You can decline or change your choice in Cookie settings.' Replace the anonymous claim with 'If enabled with your permission, optional analytics collects limited technical and usage information. It is not used for advertising. Appointment-form fields are not included in our custom analytics events.' Publish this only after confirming those operational statements. The fact of browsing a condition page is not proof that the visitor has that condition; no ad-platform disclosure is asserted here.
seo_aeo: Searchable health content stays intact. Use aggregated, non-sensitive site reporting rather than individual health-topic attribution; do not sacrifice privacy for campaign granularity.
client_input: GA enhanced-measurement settings, campaign naming rules, processor/retention settings and confirmation that no advertising linkage is enabled.

status: Confirmed reachable logging branch; actual activation/log contents not inspected
title: The missing-email-key fallback writes full appointment details into server logs
quoted_text: console.warn('[booking] RESEND_API_KEY not set, request not emailed.\n' + mail.text); mail rows include 'Patient name', 'Mobile', 'Age', 'Guardian' and appointment details.
why: The fallback has no development-only guard and serializes personal appointment data to logging infrastructure if the email key is absent, contrary to the requested no-personal-data-in-logs control.
alternative: Remove mail.text and all submitted values from log messages. If email delivery is not configured, return a neutral failure with the existing phone/WhatsApp options instead of logging personal information and showing success. Allow only a generic operational error code or random non-personal correlation identifier in logs. Confirm that error reporting also redacts request bodies/provider payloads. Do not submit real patient details to test this path; use isolated synthetic tests.
seo_aeo: No impact on public search content. A truthful booking failure is preferable to a false successful submission and an unnecessary personal-data copy.
client_input: Deployment owner confirms email configuration, logging access/retention and redaction. No secrets, inboxes, existing logs or submissions were accessed, and no real leak is claimed.
